title: Finite dimensional twisted sections for the canonical base-field action
statement: Put A=k[x_0,x_1] with its total-degree grading, P=Proj A [def-sc-p1-standard], and let rho:k -> Gamma(P,O_P) be the composite sending c to C(c) in A_0, then to Gamma(Spec A_0,O) via the inverse affine global-sections isomorphism, then to Gamma(P,O_P) by the pullback of Proj.toSpecZero. Scalars act on sections by restriction along rho. Let G be a coherent O_P-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For every integer n, Gamma(P,G tensor O_P(n)) [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] is finite-dimensional over k for this specified action.

source.place: Stacks Project, Lemma 01YS(3) and proof of (5), https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YS; online text read

proof.text: The degree-one opens D_+(x_0) and D_+(x_1) cover polynomial Proj. The homogeneous-fraction description of O(n) gives a rank-one trivialization on each open, for every integer n. Locally, tensoring G with this rank-one free module is isomorphic to G, so it preserves finite type and the finite-type kernel condition defining coherence. Thus G tensor O(n) is coherent. Polynomial Proj is Noetherian, and a coherent module on it is quasi-coherent and finitely presented.

Use proj_shifted_free_is_twist to identify polynomial Proj with the glued projective line and O(n) with the transported glued twist. Transport G tensor O(n) to a coherent module on that line. Apply finiteDimensional_H in degree zero and H.zeroLinearEquiv to its global sections. The chart maps carry constants to C(c)/1, so the scalar structure of this equivalence is precisely restriction along rho. Transport finite dimensionality back along the linear equivalence. Zero G gives dimension zero; all integer twists use the same local argument.
